transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or sent the wrong version to a client. Even when I can see it’s probably fine, I just keep going back over it in my mind.
When those thoughts show up, do you feel driven to check your work over and over to try to relieve the anxiety?

Yes. Before I submit something, I’ll reopen the file, compare the layers, save it again, and sometimes go through every design choice in my head one more time. It doesn’t take up my whole day, but it makes me slower and less able to just move on creatively.
Do you feel that the amount of checking you do is excessive, even though it’s hard to stop?

Yes, I think it probably is more than I need to do. I’ll reopen the file, compare the layers, save it again, and go through the choices in my head. It doesn’t take over my whole day, but it does slow me down and makes it harder to just move on creatively.
Do these thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted to you?

Yes. I don’t want to keep thinking about it, but I’ll get this worry that I missed some tiny thing in a layout or sent the wrong version, and my mind just keeps circling back to it even when I can see it’s probably fine.
Do these unwanted checking thoughts also happen in other parts of your life besides your design work?
Mostly it’s around my design work—the worry that I missed a tiny mistake or sent the wrong version. Even when I know it’s probably fine, I keep going back over it in my mind.
If you try not to recheck your work, can you stop yourself?

I can sometimes stop myself, but it’s hard. Before I submit something, I usually feel like I need to reopen the file, compare the layers, save it again, and go over the design choices in my head. If I try not to, I feel unsettled and worry I’ve missed something.
Outside of your design work, are you generally a perfectionistic person?
I’m not sure I’d say I’m generally perfectionistic. It’s mostly something I notice with my design work.
Do these checking habits feel unreasonable to you?

I mean, I know I probably don’t need to do all of it. But before I submit, I still reopen the file, compare the layers, save it again, and go through the choices in my head. It doesn’t take over my whole day, but it makes me slower and less able to just move on creatively.
When you reopen and recheck the file, does it reduce the anxiety for a while?

Yeah, for a little while. Once I’ve reopened it, checked the layers, and saved it again, I feel more settled. But then the next time I’m about to submit something, I tend to feel like I need to do it all over again.
Did these worries and rechecking habits start after a particular stressful event at work?
No, I can’t really point to one particular stressful event. It’s more something I gradually started noticing with work.
Does this checking feel unlike the kind of person you want to be?

Yeah. I’m still getting my work done, but it’s not really how I want to work. I’ve missed some internal deadlines because I keep checking, and I hold back on bolder ideas because I’m worried I’ll overlook something. It makes me feel like I’m getting in my own way, especially with trying to move toward a creative director role.
Do you ever get other unwanted thoughts that keep intruding on you, aside from worries about mistakes in your design work?

Mostly it’s still about work—these nagging thoughts that I missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or that I sent the wrong version to a client. Even when I can see it’s probably fine, my mind just keeps circling back to it.
Do these thoughts and checking habits feel unwanted to you?
Yes. I don’t want them there. I’ll look at the layout and know it’s probably fine, but I still get this thought that I missed some tiny error or sent the wrong file, and it just keeps coming back.
Do these checking habits feel out of character for you?

Yeah, it does. Before submitting something, I’ll reopen the file, compare the layers, save it again, and sometimes go through every design choice in my head. It’s not taking over my whole day, but it makes me slower and less creatively free than I want to be.
When you have the thought that you may have missed a mistake, do you believe the fear is probably exaggerated?

Yes, most of the time I know it’s probably exaggerated. I can look at the layout and see it seems fine, but I still can’t quite let go of the thought that I missed something small or sent the wrong version.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about several different areas of life, not just your design work?
I’m not sure I’d say it’s across several areas of my life. It’s mostly around my design work and getting things right before I send them.
Do these checking rituals feel like something you wish you could stop?

Yes. I wish I could just submit it once I’ve checked it and move on. Instead I reopen the file, compare the layers, save it again, and go over the choices in my head. It’s not all day, but it slows me down and makes me feel less creatively free.
Has this pattern of repeatedly checking and doubting your work been present since early adulthood?

Yes, it’s been there since early adulthood. Before I submit something, I tend to reopen the file, compare the layers, save it again, and mentally go through the design choices one more time. It doesn’t take over my whole day, but it definitely makes me slower and less creatively free.
Do these checking habits feel alien to you, like they don’t fit with your values or the way you want to work?

Yes. I want to be able to trust my work and send it when it’s ready, but I end up reopening the file, checking the layers, saving again, and going through the choices in my head. It makes me slower and less free creatively.
Do these repeated checking urges feel senseless to you?

Yes, mostly. I know I’ve already checked the work, but I still feel like I need to reopen it, compare the layers, save it again, and go through the choices in my head. It’s not taking over my whole day, but it does slow me down and make me feel less free creatively.
